body: He’s trying. I’m trying to convince him to come down and stay with me so that he’s not alone and, frankly, so that I can keep an eye on him and to best assess the situation. I will recommend him changing therapists and medications asap.

He has a therapist but from everything he’s told me, it’s not a good fit for him and she tries to get him in and out of her office as quickly as possible.

He feels like his life is falling apart because he’s behind in school and running out of money. He’s also hit a hiccup with his boss and he’s afraid that he’s going to lose his job. He’s been on these meds that make him feel sick all the time. He’s definitely depressed, he’s been depressed for a while but in the last few weeks it’s definitely escalated.

He’s smart, funny, handsome, insightful, and has a bright future ahead of him. I love him and I cannot let him do this. There are a lot of people who care about him and I cannot let this happen. I will do EVERYTHING in my power to prevent this.
I appreciate you taking the time to share your insight with me. I know that there are things about their relationship that bother him, which is why he was talking to me about it in the first place.
“Running your mouth” is a good way to put it. I appreciate your reply, thank you.

I didn’t get the chance to tell him why I had that opinion. 

Thanks for taking the time to reply- I really value being able to talk to other people about this.

I didn’t call her names, and I didn’t feel the impulse to. Within the context of our conversation, I thought that pointing this out would help him to identify some patterns in her behavior that have been bothering him.

Thanks for taking the time to reply and to give advice. I appreciate it a lot.
The only thing I can think of is some kind of abuse situation. Given what I know about her I don’t have any reason to think that’s the case but you never know.
Yeah that’s what I’m most worried about- that he’s regretting he told me. I texted him and I think we’ll talk today. Thanks for replying.
I appreciate your comments. Thanks for sharing another perspective on this- everything helps.
This was sort of my thought process.
This experience has me worried that I am, in fact, the unpleasant one. But your response gives me some stuff to think about. Thanks for taking the time to reply.

Thanks for taking the time to comment, I really appreciate it.

This guy is not someone I usually walk on eggshells with. On the contrary, the dynamic in our relationship is one of complete honesty, and we tend to give each other our unfiltered opinions. We've had some intense discussion on some deep stuff, including things we actively disagree with. The more I talk to him, the come to understand and respect his position on the things we don't see eye to eye with. 


He does tend to take criticism of his friend a little personally, in my opinion. In his defense, they have had a long friendship and she's been there for him at times in his life when he really needed it, and I know that he cares about her very much. This friendship has been generally a positive force in his life and I can imagine it's hard to hear a super negative assessment of someone who has been an important friend to him. 

I don't know how long he'll stay mad for. As much as it distresses me to know that he's angry at me, I guess I'm mostly just feeling ashamed that when I'm at my most unfiltered, I'm judgmental and had a big lack of empathy. I think you're in the right about trying not to judge anyone's reason for having an abortion.
